messages:
Maya Patel: Hey team, incoming escalation from Acme Ops — they report a regression in p95/p99 for the tool-calling path. /v1/chat.func_call p95 moved from ~280ms to ~1.9s around 11:02 PST, p99 ~3.1s. No error spike, just latency. They include a repro (small prompt + function call sequence). Sharing logs in thread. Can someone pick up triage? :eyes:

Sam Chen: cc @eng-runtime @eng-sre. I can take initial triage. Do we have correlating infra events?

Maya Patel: No infra alerts. Customer saw it in prod starting ~11:02. They said it affects only routes that use structured output + router-based tool dispatch (JSON schema validation turned on).

infra-bot: Trace link: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/abcd1234 (sample span highlights: tool_router -> schema_validator -> kernel_exec).

David Liu: Looking at traces now. I see a clear hot path: tool_router.execRequest shows a large CPU wait inside schema_validation.validateSchema for the customer traces. Median validation time jumped from ~4ms to ~220ms for validated payloads. The router queue depth also increased briefly.

Elena Garcia: Customer repro steps attached: small prompt -> assistant asks to call weather API -> tool router selects external_tool.weather -> payload validated against the JSON schema (with nested enums + multipleOf checks). They say turning off validation restores the previous latency.

Sam Chen: Useful repro. Two immediate hypotheses: 1) a recent change to the JSON Schema validator (was updated last week) introduced slower code paths for certain schema constructs; 2) router is doing redundant validation + canonicalization for each retry/route.

Rajesh Kumar: I'm seeing an infra-side correlation: a canary rollout of router v2.11 (id: rtr-2.11-canary) started at 10:50 and finished 10:59 across one region. The canary had a rebuilt schema-validator module (node native addon) — maybe it's slower in some workloads.

David Liu: Confirmed. Canary traces map to the same commit that replaced our incremental validator with a strict recursive validator to fix correctness issues. Good for correctness but heavier for nested enums/oneOf combos.

Maya Patel: Customer is on Hosted tier but high throughput, they're sensitive to p99. They asked for mitigation now. What can we do quickly?

Sam Chen: Short-term mitigations: 1) disable JSON schema validation per-customer (config toggle) for affected routes; 2) route them to older router binary (rollback canary) for this region; 3) increase router worker pool temporarily. We should prefer non-invasive options first.

David Liu: I can patch the router to short-circuit schema validation for requests that attach a validated signature header (we already emit those for cached tool results). That would be a quick path but needs a tiny release (hotfix).

Rajesh Kumar: I'll roll back the rtr-2.11 canary in the affected region if you want immediate mitigation. Doing rollback now will take ~3-5min to drain.

Elena Garcia: Customer asked if we can do anything immediately without changing model output. They can disable strict validation on their side but prefer us to keep validation enabled. They asked for ETA and whether there is potential correctness regression if we turn validation off here.

Sam Chen: For immediate safety, we can toggle per-tenant validation off for that specific route; that'll avoid correctness checks but the router will still dispatch tools. We'll document that this increases risk of malformed tool payloads reaching downstream tools.

Maya Patel: Customer agreed to temporary toggle if it restores latency. Please add clear rollback and a TTL for the setting.

David Liu: Proposed quick action plan: 
- Action A (Immediate): Rajesh roll back router canary in region us-west-2 (impact: ~3-5min).
- Action B (Immediate): I will prepare a hotfix to add a fast-path in schema_validator (skip expensive enum/oneOf checks for known-simple schemas) and cut a patch release (rtr-2.11.1).
- Action C (Short window): Add per-tenant toggle: enable_json_schema_validation: false for customer acme-ops for the affected route with TTL 2 hours.

Rajesh Kumar: Rolling back canary now. Watch logs: deploy-bot: rollback rtr-2.11-canary -> rtr-2.10-stable.

infra-bot: Deploy started at 11:12:08, expected drain 180s.

David Liu: I'm starting the hotfix branch. Minimal change: restore the previous incremental validator code for the heavy code paths but keep strict checks in unit tests. Will try to get a patch out in ~90 minutes.

Sam Chen: I've toggled the per-tenant flag for acme-ops on the control plane: 
```
tenant_configs.set("acme-ops", "enable_json_schema_validation", false, ttl=7200)
```
Customer confirms latency dropped to baseline within 2 minutes after toggle. p99 back to ~310ms, p95 ~290ms.

Elena Garcia: Customer extremely grateful and provided logs showing the improved response times. They asked for a timeline for a permanent fix and whether this will affect other tenants.

David Liu: Permanent fix plan: Merge hotfix (rtr-2.11.1) with optimized validator. Add regression tests covering nested enums/oneOf. Backport to rtr-2.11 in next stability patch. Expected to complete QA + rollout in 48h.

Rajesh Kumar: I'll schedule a regional rollout after QA. Also adding an automated monitor: any large delta in validator span (median > 50ms) will trigger an alert and auto-rollback for that region.

Maya Patel: Created a support ticket SR-2026-9847 and linked the customer acceptance confirmation. Marking priority P1 until hotfix is released.

Sam Chen: Followups: 
- David to PR hotfix and tag for canary tomorrow morning.
- Rajesh to add metric-based safety gates (validator span threshold) to deploy pipeline.
- Elena to send customer postmortem + note about toggle and expected fix ETA.

David Liu: Drafted PR: https://git.internal.redwood/p/rtr/commit/7f9b2a (internal). Includes perf benches: running our schema suite shows ~90% reduction on heavy schemas vs the strict validator.

Elena Garcia: Customer asked whether we can expose a safe-mode that does lightweight structural checks (shapes only, no deep enums/multipleOf) to avoid toggling off entirely. Is that feasible?

David Liu: Yes — we will add a "validation_profile": ["strict","shape-only","off"] option per-route. Shape-only will skip deep enum/oneOf and numeric multipleOf checks. That will be in rtr-2.11.1.

Maya Patel: Recording next steps in the SR: include repro, traces, rollback timeline, hotfix PR link, and TTL for the toggle. Closing the active escalation on the customer side once patch is rolled and we have a plan.

Sam Chen: Thanks all. Quick note for postmortem: call out that merging a correctness-focused validator without targeted perf benchmarks on common schema patterns caused the p99 hit. We'll add perf gate. :pray:

infra-bot: SR-2026-9847 updated: status=mitigated, mitigations=[rollback_canary, per-tenant-toggle], next_steps=[hotfix_PR, deploy_safety_gates].

Maya Patel: I'll follow up with the customer in ~2 hours with an update and ETA. Closing thread here for now.

Sam Chen: closing from infra/triage side, will reopen if anything else comes up. :wave:
